title: Cabinet backed a constitutional move to extend the retirement age of superior court judges by two years.
body_paragraphs: The professional body representing around 26,000 lawyers unanimously opposed the plan at a special general meeting, warning of damage to public confidence in judicial independence. Its office-bearers then met the minister in charge and sought an appointment with the head of state to convey the resolution and an earlier study on court delays.

Party leaders from across the aisle held an unusually broad meeting and agreed to intensify scrutiny inside and outside the legislature. Separately, the association requested that any measure affecting judicial tenure be tested against provisions on people’s sovereignty (the constitution’s Articles 3 and 4) and, if necessary, put to a referendum (a nationwide vote of the electorate).

title: The United States launched a Public Health Pest Control and Vector‑Borne Disease Response program with Sri Lanka’s Health Ministry.
body_paragraphs: Experts from US Army Pacific and the 18th Theater Medical Command began training local units in preventive medicine, entomology (the study of insects), disease surveillance, and integrated vector management. The initiative supported nationwide efforts during one of the worst dengue years in recent memory, with more than 80,000 cases recorded by late July and daily averages exceeding 2,000 earlier in the month.

The effort complemented military-to-military cooperation such as CARAT and Atlas Angel and a separate pledge by Australia of AUD 2 million for a Wolbachia project (a bacterium-based mosquito control method). The embassy said the goal was to build sustainable capabilities that outlast the current outbreak.

title: Cabinet approved procurement for Phase I of the Ruwanpura Expressway at an estimated Rs. 15 billion.
body_paragraphs: The section spans from Kahathuduwa to Ingiriya, including a system interchange linking to the Southern Expressway. The roads authority aims to complete the tendering and award the contracts within 2026, with financing drawn from domestic budget allocations for the year.

Officials said the decision included selecting a suitable contractor through a competitive process overseen by the line ministry. The project’s first phase is intended to improve connectivity to population centers south‑east of Colombo.

title: Sri Lanka and India reviewed Indian‑funded projects and agreed to set up a monitoring unit at the Presidential Secretariat.
body_paragraphs: A deputy minister met the envoy in Colombo to discuss bottlenecks affecting schemes across transport, ports and aviation, water, housing, plantation and community infrastructure, fisheries, science and technology, justice, and national integration. The talks also covered a US$ 450 million loan‑and‑grant package for disaster recovery and reconstruction.

Participants included the president’s chief of staff, the treasury secretary, and senior officials from the fisheries portfolio. The Indian side was represented by the deputy high commissioner and first secretaries for political and commercial affairs.

title: Sri Lanka and the United States conducted the sixth CARAT maritime exercise in Trincomalee and Colombo.
body_paragraphs: Shore and sea phases covered maritime domain awareness, tactical medicine, explosive ordnance disposal, and VBSS (visit, board, search and seizure) operations. A P‑8A Poseidon supported surveillance drills, while a US Coast Guard maritime team trained aboard SLNS Gajabahu using a rigid‑hull inflatable boat.

Organizers said the week‑long program aimed to improve interoperability for search and rescue, disaster response, and regional security missions in the Indian Ocean. Community projects and sports activities complemented operational training.

title: The debt office offered Rs. 250 billion in T‑bonds across four maturities for the July 30 auction.
body_paragraphs: The tranches comprised 2031 (Rs. 90 billion, 11.60% coupon), 2034 (Rs. 80 billion, 11.70%), 2036 (Rs. 50 billion, 10.85%) and 2037 (Rs. 30 billion, 10.75%). Ahead of the sale, secondary‑market yields were largely anchored, with 01.08.2030 trading between 11.60% and 11.68% and 15.01.2033 near 12.27%.

On the currency side, the rupee hovered around Rs. 336.25 per US dollar, little changed from earlier quotes. Banking‑system overnight liquidity expanded to about Rs. 174 billion from roughly Rs. 163 billion.

title: The national carrier entered an interline agreement with Island Aviation Services to connect 17 Maldivian destinations.
body_paragraphs: Travelers can book a single electronic ticket for journeys via Malé and Gan, combining international legs with domestic hops operated by the partner. The move expands access to outer atolls while simplifying itineraries for both leisure and corporate segments.

The airline currently runs three daily services to the Maldivian capital and two weekly to Gan. Officials said the tie‑up should also support agents and tour operators through easier ticketing and through‑check arrangements.

title: Police recorded 22 shootings so far this year, with 15 fatalities and 12 injuries.
body_paragraphs: A spokesperson linked many incidents to rival narcotics networks, contract hits and intimidation attempts. Ten cases occurred within a two‑week window in mid‑July, including a fatal attack near a popular walking track and a killing at a birthday event.

Investigators said communications analysis and human‑source intelligence were being used to identify planners and gunmen, some allegedly operating from abroad. Arrests were made within an hour in one suburban case, with the suspected rider and shooter held.

title: Consumer Affairs Authority filed cases against 23 private hospitals and labs over expired medical goods, with fines totaling about Rs. 5.8 million.
body_paragraphs: Inspections found expired chemicals used in diagnostics, out‑of‑date medicines kept for patient care and sales, and charges above regulated prices for laboratory tests. Some facilities stored expired items alongside usable stock, breaching separation norms.

The regulator said additional prosecutions are pending and urged reports via hotline 1977 during office hours. It warned that misleading or unsafe practices risk market‑access restrictions and further court action.

title: The United States set Sri Lanka’s tariff at 10% under a forced‑labour import review, avoiding a higher bracket.
body_paragraphs: Industry groups said the outcome preserves parity with key apparel competitors where a 2.5‑percentage‑point gap can swing orders. The finance ministry credited a recent prohibition on goods made with forced labour for helping secure the lower rate.

The decision follows a global Section 301 process and replaces earlier emergency surcharges struck down by the US Supreme Court (the top judicial body in the United States). Exporters to that market said certainty on duty lines aids pricing and contract discussions.

title: Cabinet cleared disposal of accumulated SLTB scrap metal to six firms for roughly Rs. 195.89 million.
body_paragraphs: Awards went to Ashok Steel Industries, S.R. Steel, IWW Steel Industries, Udaya Industries, Kalana Tech Engineering, and Ceylon Steel Casting based on a high‑level committee’s recommendation. The materials included obsolete inventory from depots across the network.

Officials said the sale reduces maintenance costs tied to storage while generating non‑fare revenue for the bus sector. Proceeds are to be credited through standard treasury channels after completion of handover formalities.
